episode_title: Marketing your dispensary for Green Wednesday, Black Friday and beyond – Part 3

real_qa.q: How can cannabis dispensaries use bundling strategy to increase sales during Green Wednesday and Black Friday while managing inventory constraints?
real_qa.r: Dispensaries can create bundles combining popular brands with less popular brands and cheaper items to create perceived value without deep discounting. Accessories like papers and glassware can be added to bundles to avoid impacting daily or monthly purchase limits while increasing total basket value. This strategy allows retailers to move slower-moving inventory by leveraging popular products as anchors, similar to how McDonald's bundles low-margin burgers with high-margin fries and beverages.
real_qa.requete: cannabis dispensary bundling strategy Black Friday

real_qa.q: What marketing approach should independent cannabis dispensaries take on Small Business Saturday to compete against MSOs?
real_qa.r: Independent dispensaries should avoid competing with larger MSO brands on Green Wednesday and Black Friday deals, instead focusing promotional efforts on Small Business Saturday (typically Saturday or extended through Sunday). They should emphasize their local ownership story, partner with other nearby small businesses and locally-owned brands, and educate customers about the community economic impact of supporting local businesses. Video content and transparent narratives about why they started and what they're up against are critical to converting local preference into sales.
real_qa.requete: Small Business Saturday cannabis dispensary local marketing

real_qa.q: How does dispensary location proximity compare to brand loyalty and discounts in driving customer purchase decisions?
real_qa.r: Actual customer behavior data shows that proximity to home or work is the most important factor driving dispensary choice, more significant than brand loyalty or discounts. Scatter map analysis reveals huge concentrations of customers visiting dispensaries located near their residences or workplaces, even when they claim to prioritize brands or discounts. This geographic convenience factor is especially important for small dispensaries in areas that might otherwise be underserved.
real_qa.requete: cannabis customer dispensary location vs brand loyalty

real_qa.q: What online strategy can cannabis retailers implement on Cyber Monday to combat shopping fatigue and repeat customer visits?
real_qa.r: Retailers can adopt a flash-deal model inspired by sites like meh.com, offering a new deal every single day or rotating product deals every hour to drive repeated site visits and time-compressed purchasing decisions. Another tactic is printing customized coupons on Green Wednesday and Black Friday receipts that are valid exclusively for Cyber Monday online orders, with staff trained via documented standard operating procedures to inform customers about the future redemption opportunity.
real_qa.requete: Cyber Monday cannabis online sales strategy flash deals

real_qa.q: How should cannabis dispensaries leverage Giving Tuesday charitable partnerships to strengthen brand alignment and community engagement?
real_qa.r: Dispensaries should select charitable causes that genuinely align with organizational values and tell the story behind why the partnership matters, rather than assuming customers understand the connection. Tactics include partnering with animal rescue organizations to feature adoptable puppies and kittens, or working with occupational training and reentry charities to host art auctions and sales, creating attendance incentives beyond charity messaging itself. The narrative around the cause—especially for organizations helping people reentered society after drug-related convictions—must be explicitly communicated to resonate with customers.
